So, I almost forgot about the little project I was working on, talked about in this post. And I have a few questions, and hope to spark discussions, with general game design.

"Will" saves/checks, or resisting having your mind taken over and being helpless to attack your friends. I've been stuck of that should be a Wisdom roll, or a Spirit roll (Spirit being Charisma in DnD terms, with a few changes that makes it not completely terrible.)

Secondly, skills. How much should they overlap? Should someone with a high medical skill be able to make a healing potion, despite having 0 ranks in alchemy? I feel like it should because it lets PCs just do more things. But on the other hand, I feel like it shouldnt, because then you could out potentially do exactly what someone else can do, but without specializing in. And do other things as well.

Thirdly, HP. The sort of system that Im designing has the number 8 it's average number. The average HP is 8, and that can be increased by both Constitution and Strength (To a lesser degree). And you can increase it further by adding skill ranks to "Endurance" which will increase it per rank. "Average" endurance would be 1 rank, and most fighters would have 3+ endurance. A character can have a grand total of 5 at level 1. The maximum endurance one could possibly have is 15, which is only achievable at max level, and utterly maxing it out on each and every level. (Keeping in mind, maxing out skills is a very costly thing to do, and specilizing in skills completely can interfere with your other skills.)

With this in mind, the max level is 10. Should PCs be given an extra max HP every level, or every odd level?

And lastly, diplomacy. What I've been thinking about is tossing the normal diplomacy roll, and rather have "demeanor's" such as Intimidation, Authoritarian, Diplomatic, Flirtatious, ect. They chose a select amount, and when they want to specifically talk to someone with the goal of changing their attitude, they will evoke a demeanor, and use it how they will. Thoughts?

I think for the will save at least, you should go with a "spirit" roll. I feel its a better translation for will. A stronger spirit I think makes more sense to resist mind control than stronger wisdom - which to me translates more for knowledge/active magic checks. You might want to consider differentiating between active and passive skill checks that way too.

For skills - keep it simple - or rather think of it this way - would a highly skilled surgeon be able to work as a pharmacist or chemist? Nope. You could do like some games do and offer a "discount" on taking a package of related skills - so as to find the means to your goal of having PCs do more, but also not be able to circumvent something they really shouldn't be able to do.

With 8 HP at the absolute middle ( I'm guessing 7 max at each side?) and max level is ten, then you should probably keep it every odd level. That'd make a base increase of 5 if they only increased their Con ranks appropriately. . . It really just depends on how HP is going to be awarded with leveling up. Is there a base everyone gets despite raising their ranks? Are ranks on a point-buy system?

I like the idea of demeanors... It's like taking diplomacy and giving everyone a class type in it. Some situations should be better aided by certain demeanors. I think it might work best if PCs had to choose a couple demeanors they can do at all, and then choose to spend points in them according to how they are building their character.

Oh, sorry. I should have explained HP a bit more, although I will probably play test it twice. One with HP given every level, and another time with HP given at every odd level. But, Ill try to explain it.

Each time you level up, you gain skill ranks based on Intelligence, and then you just spend them like skill points in DnD or Pathfinder. Outside of HP increasing skills (Endurance) there are very few ways to increase HP outside of just leveling up. So, someone with completely average stats would have 8 HP. 1 Rank in endurance would add +1 in HP which would be 9 Total HP. Said PC levels up, and then takes some skill ranks to add 2 ranks to endurance. This would have a total of 3 ranks of endurance, which would be +3 HP. 8+3 = 11 HP.

This is designed so that each drop of HP actually matters, if the "average" Hp is 8 or so. And thus, makes PCs much more human. One handed weapons will deal an average of 4-5, depending on a lot of other things. Getting into fights at level 1 isn't really an option, except to the Fighter. Because he will most likely have badass combat abilities to everyone else (He'd still be an apprentice fighter, compared to the rest of the world though)

On the topic of demeanors, I plan to have quite a few of them. Maybe somewhere around 12-20. Some of them would overlap at 20 no doubt, but It's just to make sure that even with a large 8 person party or some thing, there can still be people with different demeanors.

Or maybe, I could have a few of them, and have sub-specializations out of the "main" ones, much like you suggested. Ill have to see how it turns. out.

Thank you for the feedback.
